notes.overview: 13.626 km, 38 turns, WEC layout -- by far the longest in the roster, and losing focus over the lap length is itself a common mistake. ABS activation is a recurring GT3 risk through the Dunlop and Ford chicanes: brake early and straight rather than trail-braking hard. Hypercar's main differentiator is hybrid-torque wheelspin on exits (Tertre Rouge, both Mulsanne chicanes) rather than different lines, plus energy management across the three long straights. Common mistakes: overdriving the chicane braking zones, aggressive kerbs through the Porsche Curves, early throttle at Tertre Rouge and Arnage, and fading concentration late in the lap.

corners.1: Use the track and kerb on the left for entry, late apex staying close to the right, light lift if needed.
corners.2-3: Heavy uphill braking, brake early and straight (ABS intervention is common in GT3 -- don't brake too deep into it), use the left kerb for rotation instead of aggressive trail-braking; on the right-hand exit, straighten the car before throttle and use all the exit kerb (track limits).
corners.4-5: A high-speed right (flat out, tight to the right on exit), a medium-speed left with smooth steering, then a right-hand continuation that balances the car before throttle to set up Tertre Rouge -- don't run wide.
corners.6: Critical right-hander onto the Mulsanne straight, light braking, late apex, cut the inside kerb, traction is everything (no wheelspin) -- a poor exit costs seconds on the straight.
corners.7: One of the hardest braking zones, brake early and straight between 100-75 m, careful downshifting to avoid rear instability, inside kerbs on entry; exit is a left-right sequence prioritizing traction over aggression.
corners.8: Similar braking around 75 m with a slight camber change, conservative brakes, slight kerb cut; on exit, straighten the car and use the full width before applying throttle past the right-hander's apex.
corners.9: Tight right-hander, brake early, rotate first and throttle second -- rear tyres overheat easily here.
corners.10: High-speed kink taken under braking, brake in a straight line before turn-in, stability is critical.
corners.11: Left-hand corner, late apex, don't over-rotate; the downhill exit needs gentle throttle (rear instability is common in GT3).
corners.12: The slowest corner on the circuit, heavy braking at the second board, very late apex, don't run wide on exit, short-shift if traction is poor -- the exit defines the next straight.
corners.13: A minor bend, not important, don't overuse steering.
corners.14-16: T14: fast right, light lift. T15: high-speed double-left -- aero balance matters, running wide means the wall; mid-apex first, late apex second. T16: long right using full width, lift early then reapply throttle, tight at the end to open Karting.
corners.17: Fast left, just a light brake tap, maintain rhythm -- any correction costs speed, inside kerbs are cuttable.
corners.18-19: Heavy braking at the start of the kerb, use the full track to the right, cut the kerbs on entry with straight steering (ABS activation likely); stay right afterward to set up Ford Chicane 2.
corners.20-21: The slowest chicane on the track -- cut the first kerb a little if the car is stable, smooth steering; use the flat kerbs mid-corner and on exit, avoid the sausage kerb/gravel, late apex for a clean run onto the main straight.
